title: MONDAY STORMS
full_story:
Severe storms came through Clay County last night, resulting in tornado and severe thunderstorm warnings.  The storms produced some brief strong winds and small hail.

Clay County ESDA Director Steve Lewis reports that a large tree limb fell across some power lines on Church Street in Louisville because of the storms, but no other damage was reported.

The Association of Illinois Electric Cooperatives reports that there were scattered power outages throughout Southern Illinois.  According to their report Pope County had the most electric customers off line.

title: BROWN SENTENCED
full_story:
Clay County State’s Attorney Phillip M. Givens announced that Matthew R. Brown, 41, of Flora, was sentenced to time in the Illinois Department of Corrections on Monday, in Clay County Circuit Court for the offense of Theft, a Class 3 Felony.

The charge alleged that between May 15th, 2025, and May 17th, 2025, Brown exerted unauthorized control over property of a victim with said property having a total value exceeding $500 but not exceeding $10,000, intending to deprive the victim permanently of the use or benefit of the property.  Brown pled guilty to the offense on June 27th, 2025.  Upon completion of a contested sentencing hearing on Monday, Brown was sentenced to 7 years to the Illinois Department of Corrections by Judge Joel Powless.  Brown will have a 6-month period of Mandatory Supervised Release.

The investigation was conducted by the Flora Police Department.  State’s Attorney Phillip Givens said: “My office will continue to look out for the best interest of justice while holding people accountable for their actions.  I am grateful our law enforcement has the same outlook in protecting our community.”

title: IUKA MAN SENTENCED
full_story:
28-year-old Jacob Mann of Iuka was sentenced Friday, to 30 months’ probation and 30 days in the Marion County Jail after pleading guilty to a violation of the sex offender registry.

Mann plead guilty earlier in Marion County Court to the charge, in exchange for the dismissal of two other counts.

Mann was also ordered to undergo drug evaluation and treatment, undergo a mental health evaluation, and ordered to not use controlled substances or alcohol.  He was fined $500 and ordered to pay a $750 probation fee.

title: AMERICAN LEGION WALK
full_story:
The Flora and Louisville American Legions will be sponsoring the 3rd annual “Be The One” walk to raise public awareness to Veteran’s suicide on May 9th.

The walk will start at 8am at the Clay County World War 2 Memorial across from the Flora VFW, and end at the Clay County Veterans Monument on the Clay County Courthouse Square.  The walk will be followed by a lunch provided by the Louisville American Legion and transportation will be provided back to Flora.  Everyone is invited to attend.

Last year’s walk had 125 walkers and raised $15,000 for the cause and they hope to top that effort this year, with a goal of 250 walkers.  For more information or to register call or stop by either of the American Legion Posts.

title: NATIONAL DAY OF PRAYER
full_story:
Churches within the Clay City School District will be leading in prayer and music on the 75th Annual National Day of Prayer, Thursday, May 7th at 7:00 pm.  This year’s annual event will be hosted by the Clay City Community Southern Baptist Church (Route 50 – West of Casey’s).

The National Day of Prayer is a vital part of America’s heritage and is as relevant and critical today as it was at the first call by our Continental Congress in 1775.  Established in public law by a joint resolution of Congress, signed by President Truman in 1952, then amended to designate the day under the 100th Congress and President Reagan in 1988, it states that: “The President shall issue each year a proclamation designating the first Thursday in May as a National Day of Prayer on which the people of the United States may turn to God in prayer and meditation at churches, in groups and as individuals.”

Please join us to exercise one of our most precious freedoms For additional information, please contact Clay City Area NDP Coordinator, Pat Burt at 618-676-1783.

The Clay County Ministerial Alliance is having a National Day Of Prayer event on May 7th at 6 pm at the Flora City Hall Flagpole.  Everyone is invited to come and offer a prayer.

title: ISP TEAM ILLINOIS YOUTH POLICE CAMPS
full_story:
Illinois State Police (ISP) is now accepting applications for the three Team Illinois Youth Police Camps (TIYPC) this summer.  Each week-long, overnight camp is geared towards teenagers (ages 13-17 years) and focuses on providing personal development opportunities to challenge young people to reach their full potential.

The TIYPCs are based upon a military model and attendees, or cadets, learn military drills and participate in physical fitness exercises.  Cadets also attend classroom instruction on leadership development, substance abuse resistance, team building principles, and other life-enhancing skills.  TIYPCs promote positive rapport and interactions between law enforcement and attendees.  Other local enforcement agencies, as well as local civic organizations, have partnered with ISP to provide engagement and mentorship opportunities to develop lifelong connections with young people.

The southern TIYPC will be held at Touch of Nature in Makanda, from June 7th through 13th.  To apply, go to https://www.tiypc.org/, or contact ISP Special Agent Justin Haney at 618 534-6477 or [email protected].  Applications for Makanda will be accepted until all slots are filled.

The Metro East TIYPC will be held at Principia College in Elsah, from July 12th through 18th.  To apply, contact Sandy Voytas at [email protected] or 618-420-2804, or Master Sergeant Calvin Dye at [email protected] or 217-685-4752.  Application deadline for the Metro East location is June 19th.

The northern TIYPC will be held at Lewis University in Romeoville, IL from June 21st through 27th.  To apply, contact ISP Trooper Duane Chappell at 620 417 5892 or [email protected]. Application deadline for the Romeoville location is May 9th.

title: NEW COMPUTER SCIENCE PROGRAM
full_story:
Lake Land College is set to offer a brand-new degree program in Computer Science starting Fall 2026.  The program will equip students with a wide range of programing and software skills, preparing them for high-demand STEM careers.

By focusing on key skills such as programming, error testing and problem solving, the new program will set students on paths toward high-paying careers in software development, cybersecurity, data science and more.  According to the US Bureau of Labor Statistics, employment in these fields is projected to grow much faster than the average industry over the next 10 years, with more than 317,000 new jobs projected each year.

“We’re excited to introduce this brand-new program and create a local, affordable pathway for students to access such a rewarding career field,” Mathematics Instructor Sarah Harley said.

Students who complete the Lake Land College Computer Science program will also have the option to transfer to a university to earn a bachelor’s degree in computer science.  By starting their education at Lake Land, students can complete their first two years at a fraction of a university cost, all while enjoying small class sizes and free wraparound tutoring and support services.  In addition, most core classes in the Computer Science program are a part of the Illinois Articulation Initiative (IAI), meaning students who complete the program will have guaranteed transfer to any participating Illinois university.

“The Computer Science program is designed to ensure a seamless transfer process to any university a student wants,” Harley added.  “This is a huge advantage for students, who come out financially ahead of their peers when they take advantage of our affordable tuition for the first two years of their studies.”

The Lake Land College Computer Science program is now enrolling for Fall 2026.  To learn more about the program, contact Harley at 217-234-5289 or [email protected].

title: E15 AMENDMENT
full_story:
US House members, including a handful from Illinois, introduced an amendment to the farm bill that would provide consumers with permanent, year-round access to E15.

The proposed farm bill could be voted on by the full House this week.  More than 300 amendments were submitted.

The E15 amendment would allow year-round sales of higher ethanol-gasoline blends.  The proposed amendment also would change how biofuel-blending law exemption requests from small refiners are handled under the Renewable Fuel Standard (RFS).  The proposal also would allow the US Environmental Protection Agency to grant RFS waivers if a refinery is on the brink of economic collapse or converting to production of renewable fuel.

Illinois sponsors of the amendment include Mike Bost; Eric Sorensen; Nikki Budzinski; Mary Miller; Darin LaHood; and Robin Kelly.
